scope: Read current rational product/Horner bodies and historical borrowed candidate; no new implementation or benchmark.
finding: Current Horner adds consumed Rational values (lower = lower + coefficient). Historical NonEmptyRationalInterval::translate(&self) used borrowed endpoint addition, via translated_bounds(lower, upper, offset). Thus shared arithmetic adaptation changed value ownership and temporary lifetime despite matching finite dispatch counters.
hypothesis: A consuming translation preserving owned Rational addition may avoid the borrowed-return boundary cost. It must retain each caller's existing coefficient extraction, product/addition order, declines and proof ownership.
limits: Historical runtime regression not yet reproduced on current compiler; ownership difference is an implementation hypothesis, not proof of causation or acceptance. Existing full gate and rejection remain intact.
next_requirement: Before changing production, establish current matched controls and differential witnesses; demonstrate useful cost benefit to justify any bounded size growth. No bare unchecked ordered-endpoint API should bypass invariants.

followup_source_review.decision: No production Horner candidate introduced; historical rejection remains. A further experiment requires a current measured ownership/code-generation hypothesis.
